question.text: 'Dhanvantari Healthcare AIF' has a RECYCLING provision allowing the Manager to re-invest capital returned within the commitment period. LP commitments = INR 500 crore. After Year 2, INR 150 crore has been invested, exited at INR 180 crore and the Manager wishes to recycle the INR 150 cr of returned CAPITAL (not gains). Under a typical recycling clause, what is the Manager MOST LIKELY permitted to do?

answer.text: Recycle the INR 180 crore back into new deals including gains
Recycle only the INR 150 crore (returned capital), and only within the commitment period, subject to PPM caps
Recycle without any time or quantum limit
Recycle only after obtaining fresh LP consent and SEBI approval

explanation.text: The Logic: A typical recycling provision lets the manager re-deploy returned CAPITAL (not realised gains) into new investments, but only within a defined window (most commonly the commitment period) and subject to caps disclosed up-front in the PPM. Gains above original cost are distributed to LPs rather than recycled, since LPs expect distributions of profit. The Trap: Recycling the full INR 180 crore (option A) would sweep in gains, which is atypical and LP-unfriendly. Recycling without time or quantum limits (C) contradicts the standard PPM-cap construct. Requiring fresh LP consent AND SEBI approval (D) is stricter than market practice — recycling is normally pre-authorised in the PPM. Note: The specific concept of recycling returned capital within the commitment period and the existence of PPM recycling caps is not explicitly addressed in the cited workbook chapter (FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 120, 124, 128, 200), which covers drawdown recall, green shoe, clawback, and distributions instead. The framing above is general industry/PPM practice for AIF recycling.
